3. Seat a catalyst. Distinct voices among those arranged totems all count, including the sixth.
4. Sneak-use the Spirit Codex on the Resonator to see ghosts of any missing ring slots.
5. Totems merely near it still work exactly as they did for five voices.

chapters.title: Shatter Array
chapters.text:
Centre an Echo station in a five by five with four totems of the recipe's own attunement at the corners and an Ancestral Cache beneath.

How:
1. Place the station. Four matching totems at the corners of a five by five.
2. Put an Ancestral Cache under it.
3. The station then costs a quarter less Pulse and empties itself into the cache.
4. Entirely optional. Every station works exactly as before without it.
5. Sneak-use the Codex on the station to see the ghosts.

chapters.title: Camp hands
chapters.text:
Pattern-weavers taught the camp to keep working after the singer left. Four hands sit beside the Grove Tender: the Seal Loom, the Tide Pump, the Wind Snare and the Ward Drum.

How:
1. Raise Pulse within 8 — a Drumheart, Resonator or Ley Collector.
2. Place the hand. Each one drinks Pulse only when it actually works.
3. A held redstone stills it. A comparator reads what it is doing.
4. Rank it in Echo Attune, Bind, then Manifest. Ranked hands beat faster. Pulse per move stays the same, so the lattice feels the extra speed.
5. Open the next pages for each hand, then the walkthroughs.

chapters.title: Seal Loom
chapters.text:
A recipe is a polite request. The Seal Loom writes it onto a Recipe Seal and weaves it forever.

How:
1. Craft a Recipe Seal from a Blank Seal and paper.
2. Place the Seal Loom. Hopper ingredients into the three-by-three from the sides or top.
3. Seat the blank seal in the middle slot. Arrange the recipe in the grid.
4. Sneak-use the loom empty-handed. The seal remembers that recipe.
5. Keep matching ingredients in the grid. Every second it spends 6 Pulse and weaves one result. Rank shortens that second; Pulse per craft stays 6.

chapters.title: Tide Pump
chapters.text:
Water goes where it is asked. The Tide Pump asks both ways.

How:
1. Place tanks on both faces — Spirit Cisterns, or any fluid handler.
2. The arrow face is the front. By default it draws from the front and pushes into the back.
3. Sneak-use to reverse: now it pushes into the front.
4. Each second it moves 250 mB for 4 Pulse. Rank shortens that second; Pulse per 250 mB stays 4.
5. Click empty-handed to read the current direction. A lever pauses it.

chapters.title: Wind Snare
chapters.text:
Dropped things remember the wind. The Wind Snare calls them home.

How:
1. Place it near a farm, a shatter station, or anywhere items fall.
2. Keep 2 Pulse nearby per stack it catches, up to eight stacks a second, within 8 blocks.
3. Rank shortens that second. Pulse per stack stays 2.
4. Open it like a chest, or hopper the catch out of any face.
5. A lever pauses both the catch and the hoppers. It does not steal from other inventories.

chapters.title: Ward Drum
chapters.text:
A drum can keep the dark at the edge of camp.

How:
1. Place it where hostiles walk. It listens in an 8-block sphere.
2. Keep 8 Pulse nearby. Each second it strikes one Enemy for 4 magic and a shove. Rank shortens that second; Pulse per strike stays 8.
3. Players are never the target.
4. A lever silences it. A comparator reads 15 on a hit, 0 while it waits.
5. It is a watch, not a farm. Pair a Wake Bell if the deaths should pay Pulse back.

chapters.title: Song Thread
chapters.text:
Redstone is a shout. Song Thread is a hummed line through the air.

How:
1. Craft Song Thread from redstone and Loom Thread.
2. Place it. It carries 0 to 15 in all six directions and decays by one per block.
3. Vanilla dust, levers, plates, Song Vines and comparators all speak to it.
4. Snap song plates onto faces along the line.

A wall of thread is a wall of song. Keep the line short if you need a full 15 at the far end. For a tendril that hugs stone, see Song Vine.

chapters.title: Song Vine
chapters.text:
A Pattern-weaver's song follows the stone. Song Vine is a tendril that crawls every face of a block.

How:
1. Craft eight vines from one Song Thread and a Spirit Reed.
2. Click a solid face. The vine sits in the air cell on that face.
3. Click an existing vine with another vine to add a second face on the same cell — floor and wall, or every side of a cube.
4. Power decays by one per step, including around corners onto a neighbouring face.
5. It speaks to Song Thread, song plates, vanilla dust and comparators.

Break the block to pick up one vine per face. Relays still carry items; vines carry only the song.

chapters.title: Verse Call and Answer
chapters.text:
Sixteen verses. Two plates singing the same verse hear each other without a vine.

How:
1. Snap a Verse Call onto a face. It reads redstone from every side except its facing.
2. Snap a Verse Answer onto a face within 32 blocks, same world. It sings out of its facing.
3. Sneak-use either plate to cycle verse 1 to 16. Click empty-handed to read the verse and the strength.
4. Several Calls of one verse: the Answer takes the loudest.
5. A mismatched verse stays silent. Relays still move items; these plates move only redstone.

Air Seal in the Call, Bone Chime in the Answer. Pattern-weavers favour clocks and Storm Wing.

chapters.title: Song plates
chapters.text:
Thirteen plates. Each does one job. The facing is the output.

How:
1. Snap a plate onto a solid face, the same way you snap a relay.
2. Binary plates (Chorus, Gathering, Discord, Hush) read left and right of the facing.
3. Unary plates (Inverse, Echo, Drift, Strike, Chance, Tally, Verse) read the back.
4. Memory reads left to set and right to clear.
5. Heartbeat needs no input. Sneak-use Heartbeat, Drift or Tally to change the count.

The next pages name each plate. Pattern-weavers favour redstone, clocks and Storm Wing.

chapters.title: Chorus, Gathering, Discord, Hush
chapters.text:
Four ways two voices can agree.

How:
1. Chorus (AND) sings only when left and right are both live.
2. Gathering (OR) sings when either side is live.
3. Discord (XOR) sings when the sides disagree.
4. Hush (NAND) sings unless both sides are live.

Output is 15 or 0 from the facing. Place Song Thread on that face to carry the answer.

chapters.title: Inverse and Echo
chapters.text:
One voice, turned or carried.

How:
1. Inverse (NOT) sings while the back is quiet, and hushes when the back is live.
2. Echo (BUFFER) copies the back: live stays live.

Use Inverse to turn a Pulse Threshold into a 'too empty' alarm. Use Echo to strengthen a fading Song Thread.

chapters.title: Memory, Tally, Verse
chapters.text:
The plates that remember.

How:
1. Memory: a live left sets it; a live right clears it. Output stays until told otherwise.
2. Tally: each rising edge on the back adds one. Output 15 once the count meets the threshold. Sneak-use to cycle the threshold 1 to 8. A rising left resets the count.
3. Verse: each rising edge on the back steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and emits 4, 8, 12, 15. A comparator reads the same number.

A rite-on-a-clock loop is Memory plus Heartbeat plus a Rite Pedestal comparator.

chapters.title: Heartbeat, Drift, Strike, Chance
chapters.text:
Time, delay, a tap, a coin.

How:
1. Heartbeat pulses 15 for one tick, then rests. Sneak-use cycles 20, 40, 80, 160 ticks.
2. Drift copies the back, but only after it has stayed live for 4, 8, 16 or 32 ticks (sneak-use to cycle).
3. Strike emits one tick of 15 on a rising back, then goes quiet. The Drumheart's struck-signal language.
4. Chance flips a coin on each rising back: 15 or 0 until the back falls.

A one-second Heartbeat on a Drumheart is a 24-Pulse beat if the edge lands in tempo.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: tend a grove
chapters.text:
Goal: Automatically plant and harvest a small crop plot.

You need
A Grove Tender, seeds, suitable soil, water for crops that need it, and nearby Pulse generation.

Steps
1. Craft the Grove Tender (Earth Seal, hoe, copper, Bound Echo, planks).
2. Till a 9-by-9 of farmland (or dirt for saplings, sand for cactus). Place the tender in the middle at crop height.
3. Put a Drumheart or Resonator within 8. Hopper wheat seeds into the top.
4. Wait. It plants for 4 Pulse, then harvests and replants ripe wheat for 12, keeping one seed.
5. For trees: hopper saplings. It plants, urges growth for 16 Pulse, then takes logs and leaves above.
6. For cane: hopper sugar cane onto sand or dirt beside water. It cuts the top of a three-high stalk.
Check: a bed that plants, grows and harvests without you standing there.
Next: a Wind Snare beside it to catch anything that still drops, and a Seal Loom for the harvest.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: imprint a seal
chapters.text:
Goal: automatically craft sticks from planks.

You need
A Seal Loom, a Recipe Seal, two planks of a type that can craft sticks, and a generator within 8 blocks holding at least 6 Pulse per craft.

Steps
1. Open the Seal Loom. Put the Recipe Seal in its dedicated seal slot, outside the nine-slot crafting grid.
2. Place one plank above another in the grid, just like the crafting-table recipe for sticks. Do not use sticks as the input.
3. Close the screen. Crouch and right-click the loom with an empty hand to record the matching recipe on the seal.
4. Inspect the seal tooltip: it should name the stick recipe.
5. Supply Pulse and leave output space. The loom consumes the two planks and places four sticks in its output. The Recipe Seal remains.
6. Refill the same two grid slots to repeat. A hopper can insert items, but you still need the recipe's correct arrangement. Test a single batch before connecting bulk storage.

Check
You get four sticks, spend 6 Pulse, and keep the seal. A redstone signal pauses crafting.

If it does not work
Check the dedicated seal slot, the two vertically aligned planks, stored power and free output space. Changing ingredients does not automatically change the recorded recipe.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: a song clock
chapters.text:
Goal: give a Drumheart a steady automatic beat.

You need
A Drumheart, a Heartbeat plate, solid blocks to support the plate, and Song Thread. A Pulse Gauge is optional.

Steps
1. Place the drum on your platform. Place the Heartbeat plate on a supported face nearby.
2. Crouch and use the plate until its interval reads 20 ticks, or one second.
3. Connect the plate's output side to the drum with Song Thread.
4. Watch the drum for several beats. Its stored Pulse should increase when no machine is spending it.
5. Add a Pulse Gauge if you want to turn the stored amount into a redstone signal.

Check
A steady one-second rising edge earns 24 Pulse. Rapid pulses give less power or are ignored.

If it does not work
Check the plate's orientation, support block and output connection. Remove unintended constant power. Test the clock and drum before adding thresholds or memory plates.

Next
Read the logic pages to pause machines when their inputs or power reserves run low.

chapters.title: Dawn Stag
chapters.text: A dawn grazer that carries the old forest song in its antlers. Breed with wheat; brush adults for Dawn Velvet. Bond an adult with a Bonding Charm to ride it without a saddle.

chapters.title: Lantern Fox
chapters.text: A shy dusk forager whose tail marks safe paths. Breed with sweet berries; brush adults for Lantern Down. Bond an adult with a Bonding Charm for a lantern that follows you.

chapters.title: Mossback
chapters.text: A patient wetland gardener with a living shell. Breed with seagrass; brush adults for a naturally shed Mossback Scale. Bond an adult with a Bonding Charm for a walking saddlebag.

chapters.title: Ashbound
chapters.text: The remains of a broken fire rite. Its melee strikes briefly ignite; keep water close.

chapters.title: Rootbound
chapters.text: A grove guardian twisted by a severed ley line. Slow but sturdy; its blows root travellers briefly.

chapters.title: Reed Stalker
chapters.text: A marsh hunter concealed among spirit reeds. Fast strikes carry a short poison.

chapters.title: Shardback
chapters.text: A crystal-field scavenger armored in singing stone. Keep your distance from its heavy shove.

chapters.title: Hollow Sentinel
chapters.text: An empty watchman that still guards the ancient roads. Its touch weakens the grip of attackers.

chapters.title: Storm Moth
chapters.text: A storm-fed spirit with vast veil wings. A bright gathering of motes warns of its gust; cover breaks the attack.

chapters.title: Cinder Imp
chapters.text: A nimble ember spirit. It gathers sparks before a burning bolt; the spell never ignites terrain.

chapters.title: Mourning Bell
chapters.text: A floating relic that remembers the lost tribes. Its telegraphed chime slows; shelter interrupts the song.

chapters.title: Rift Hound
chapters.text: A hunter drawn to tears in the lattice. It closes distance quickly but cannot cross worlds by itself.

chapters.title: Echo Weaver
chapters.text: An eight-legged keeper of broken songs. Its bite slows prey without placing webs or damaging the camp.
